links.outcome: Quality, factual consistency and readability of lay summaries with versus without retrieval grounding
links.effect: RAG alone offered no benefit and could introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms; RAG plus NER degraded few-shot performance but improved readability when fine-tuned.
links.quote: Results show that NER consistently improves readability and overall quality, while RAG alone offers no benefit and can introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms.

unlisted_practices: NER-based extraction of clinically relevant findings to drive patient-friendly radiology report summaries

screen.practice: retrieval grounding and NER-based entity extraction added to LLM lay summarization
screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the effect of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and clinical named entity recognition (NER) grounding mechanisms to existing LLMs to safeguard factual consistency and readability for patient-facing lay summaries.
